key_insight: WKB analysis of backward Kolmogorov equations reveals a shared Hamiltonian structure for large deviations across weak-noise, large-volume, and long-time stochastic dynamics.
engineering_relevance: This framework supports rare-event and transition-rate estimation in noisy dynamical systems, including bistable chemical reaction models.
method: Derive Hamiltonian descriptions using WKB asymptotics.
Analyze metastability with quasipotentials and finite-noise long-time behavior with tilted generators.
Survey minimum action methods, geometric variants, and neural network techniques.
evidence_signal: These lecture notes illustrate the theory with scalar and spatially extended Schlögl models; the abstract reports no quantitative benchmarks.
watch_item: The asymptotic regimes are distinct, so approximations must be matched carefully to the system’s noise level, volume, and observation timescale.
paper_title: Large Deviations in Stochastic Dynamics: A Hamiltonian Perspective
